text:
maria: seeing p99 jump to ~1.4s on a handful of hosts in us-west-2 since the 03:10 deploy. Not all hosts, looks tenant-scoped.
jay: which component? runtime or networking?
maria: runtime. stack shows heavy KV prefix miss churn and a lot of kernel fallback logs.
alex: I saw that too in metrics: per-tenant token throughput down ~40% for tenant-42. KV hitrate dropped from 92% -> 12% over ~6 minutes.
priya: oh no. any config changes in the deploy? I rolled the kernel-selection tweak last night (enable_tiered_kernels=true) and bumped default batching window to 25ms.
maria: confirmed enable_tiered_kernels= true in the release. also I noticed tenant-42 had an eviction spike from TTL priming.
jay: eviction spike? tenant-specific TTL?
alex: tenant-42 had an opt-in debugging flag enabled (kv.prefix_ttl_override_ms=30000) for a perf test. That was accidentally left on in prod for a small subset.
priya: ack. that TTL is way too low for noisy prefix patterns. It forces repeated repopulation and changes kernel selection due to sequence length profile changes.
maria: profiler snippet attached:
```
[profile] host i-0a1b2c3d: kernel_fallbacks: 47% -> logged fallback path large-kernel
[stack] runtime: /serve/kernel_selector.cpp:241
[metric] kv_prefix_evictions: +18k/min

Flame: heavy time spent in kv::populate_prefix + lock contention on shard-67
```
deploy-bot: deploy 2027-03-09T03:10:12Z started by priya (release/enable-tiered-kernels).
observability-bot: alert: kv_prefix_hitrate_drop tenant=tenant-42 severity=high at 03:16:02Z.
maria: can we confirm tenant footprint? Is tenant-42 a hot/noisy test tenant?
alex: yes, it's a partner load test. They pushed a spike of short contexts with high prefix variability. Combined with TTL override it caused continuous repopulation and eviction thrash.
jay: hypoth: tiered kernel selector sees shorter sequences (cache cold) and picks smaller-kernel fast path, then cache warms and fallback to large kernels for long context -> frequent kernel switches cause additional latency and scheduling jitter.
priya: steps: 1) revert tenant TTL override for tenant-42 2) if that doesn't stabilize, rollback enable_tiered_kernels 3) temporarily increase shard cache reservations for tenant-42.
maria: doing step 1 now:
```
# api call
POST /admin/tenants/tenant-42/config
{ "kv": { "prefix_ttl_ms": 600000 } }
```
maria: applied, observed immediate reduction in eviction rate on host i-0a1b2c3d in metrics. KV hitrate recovering from 12% -> 68% within 90s.
alex: p99 latency falling back towards baseline. Nice. But we still see kernel_fallback logs at a lower rate.
jay: kernel chatter probably because the batching window bump to 25ms increased micro-batch size variance. Larger batches shift runtime memory and cache pressure. We should tune batching heuristics to be workload-aware.
priya: opened issue with the runtime team to add tenant-weighted batching caps and prefer-stable-kernel flag per tenant: https://rwinf.atlassian.net/browse/RW-1289
maria: also, we should add a guard in the control plane to prevent TTL overrides < 60s unless opt-in for staging. Too easy to shoot prod.
alex: agree. I'll add a validation PATCH: reject prefix_ttl_ms < 60000 for prod tenants with a 409 and helpful error.
deploy-bot: rollback enable_tiered_kernels scheduled?
priya: not rolling back yet; rollback can be disruptive cluster-wide. We prefer targeted mitigations first (TTL revert + cache reservation). If CPU/GPU churn persists, we'll rollback.
maria: summary for postmortem: root cause was combination of (a) tenant-level TTL override -> extreme prefix TTL churn, (b) new batching heuristic increases variance, (c) tiered kernel selection reacts to sequence-length shifts causing kernel fallback overhead. Composite effect produced noisy-neighbor eviction spiral.
jay: mitigation: short term: disable tenant TTL override, bump per-tenant cache reservation, lower default batching window to 15ms for impacted hosts. Mid-term: add control-plane TTL validation, per-tenant kernel stability flag, and tuning for batching heuristics that avoid oscillation.
alex: prod notes: tenant-42 hitrate back to 88% in 8m, avg throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline. No SLA breaches.
priya: I'll ship small validator and the per-tenant kernel flag PR today, and propose a canary for modified batching heuristics next week.
maria: thanks all. I'll start a short incident writeup and link metrics/dashboards.
observability-bot: incident note created: incident-20270309-kv-ttl-kernel-oscillation. Dashboard: https://grafana.rwinf/board/kv-oscillations
maria: tagging @oncall for awareness and will follow up in all-hands tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
